ACT: Wake and listen toward the edge of the firelight.
Situation Description: You wake during the night after hearing movement just beyond the light of your campfire. For a moment everything goes still, but then another faint rustle comes from somewhere past the trees, close enough that it is difficult to ignore.

ACT: Listen for the distant cry again.
Situation Description: A distant cry wakes you from your rest. It sounds human, but the darkness makes it difficult to tell where it came from. The sound fades quickly, leaving you unsure whether someone nearby is injured, lost, or trying to draw attention.

ACT: Check what disturbed the supplies.
Situation Description: You wake to the sound of something shifting among your supplies beside the camp. A bag scrapes against the ground and then the noise stops, as if whatever caused it noticed that you were awake.

Situation Description: You wake and find the campfire almost extinguished, its last embers barely lighting the ground around you. The night has grown colder, and without attention the remaining glow may disappear completely.

ACT: Listen to the footsteps outside the camp.
Situation Description: Slow footsteps wake you as they approach the edge of your camp and then suddenly stop. Whoever or whatever made them is close enough to hear, but nothing enters the firelight.

ACT: Watch the moving light between the trees.
Situation Description: A faint moving light between the trees catches your attention and pulls you from sleep. It drifts for a few moments beyond the camp, disappears behind the trunks, then appears again farther away.

ACT: Listen for the animal beyond the camp.
Situation Description: A sharp animal cry breaks the silence of the night and wakes you immediately. The sound is close, followed by movement somewhere beyond the firelight, but you cannot yet tell what kind of animal is nearby.

ACT: Check where the branch broke.
Situation Description: A loud crack from somewhere nearby wakes you, followed by branches shifting in the darkness. The movement seems to continue along the tree line before suddenly going quiet.

ACT: Listen to the whispering beyond the fire.
Situation Description: You wake to quiet voices whispering somewhere beyond the edge of the firelight. The words are impossible to make out, but there is clearly more than one person nearby and they do not seem eager to be seen.

ACT: Inspect what the storm disturbed.
Situation Description: Heavy wind and rain wake you as something strikes or pulls at the edge of your camp. The shelter strains under the weather, and another sharp sound comes from the direction of your cargo.

ACT: Continue toward the source of the disturbance.
Situation Description: As you investigate, you briefly see a human-shaped figure moving between the trees, confirming that someone is nearby.

ACT: Search the immediate area one more time before giving up.
Situation Description: Your search reveals no clear tracks, person, or animal nearby.

ACT: Watch the cargo from the safety of the fire.
Situation Description: A dark shape moves beside the supplies before slipping out of view.

ACT: Continue following where the movement went.
Situation Description: The movement stops completely as soon as you approach.

ACT: Close in from the side and check the area.
Situation Description: As you circle toward the last place you heard movement, a person suddenly breaks into a run and disappears into the darkness.

ACT: Focus on the heavier sounds moving close to camp.
Situation Description: Listening carefully, you pick out slow, heavy breathing behind the earlier animal sounds. A large animal is very close.

ACT: Keep listening until the pattern of the footsteps becomes clear.
Situation Description: The rhythm resolves into careful human footsteps moving around the edge of the camp.

ACT: Check the ground and surroundings carefully.
Situation Description: As you listen, the whispering separates into two distinct voices speaking quietly just outside the firelight.

ACT: Focus on the sounds around the cargo.
Situation Description: You hear a bag scrape across the ground beside your supplies.

ACT: Stay completely still and wait for the disturbance to repeat.
Situation Description: The disturbance disappears and nothing else moves or calls out.

ACT: Wait and listen for a response to your call.
Situation Description: A frightened traveller answers your call and asks whether it is safe to approach.

ACT: Wait for the voice in the darkness to answer your challenge.
Situation Description: A tense human voice answers from the darkness and tells you not to come any closer.

ACT: Call once more and watch for a reaction.
Situation Description: Your call receives no answer, although you still sense movement nearby.

ACT: Check the ground and surroundings carefully.
Situation Description: A stranger hidden in the darkness answers your call by using your name before you have introduced yourself.

ACT: Hold position and listen for the animal's response.
Situation Description: A low growl answers your voice from beyond the firelight.

ACT: Approach the voice directly and identify who is calling.
Situation Description: You find a wounded traveller sitting against a tree and struggling to stay conscious.

ACT: Move close enough to identify the person calling for help.
Situation Description: A tired merchant steps into view and admits they became lost after nightfall.

ACT: Check the ground and surroundings carefully.
Situation Description: A lone stranger stands off the road and gives no clear reason for being there.

Situation Name: The Cry Leads to Abandoned Belongings
ACT: Search the area around the voice before stepping closer.
Situation Description: You find a pack and scattered belongings, but no person nearby.

Situation Name: Another Weak Cry Comes from Nearby
ACT: Stay quiet and listen for another cry.
Situation Description: The person calls again, much closer and noticeably weaker.

ACT: Wait and listen for the footsteps again.
Situation Description: A lone traveller slowly steps into the firelight with empty hands.

ACT: Keep following the footsteps carefully.
Situation Description: The footsteps belong to an armed stranger standing just outside the light.

Situation Name: The Footsteps Lead to a Thief
ACT: Follow the footsteps until you can see who is moving around the camp.
Situation Description: You catch a person moving quietly near the edge of your camp, clearly trying not to be seen.

Situation Name: The Whisperers Are Watching Your Camp
ACT: Keep listening without revealing yourself.
Situation Description: You realize the strangers are discussing your campsite and deciding whether to approach.

ACT: Keep listening without revealing yourself until the travellers' intent becomes clearer.
Situation Description: The voices belong to travellers arguing quietly about which road to take.

ACT: Follow the light a little farther.
Situation Description: You find a lantern that appears to have been extinguished only moments ago.

Situation Name: The Light Belongs to a Traveller
ACT: Follow the moving light until you can see who is carrying it.
Situation Description: The moving light is carried by a traveller searching for the road.

ACT: Check the ground and surroundings carefully.
Situation Description: The strange light vanishes the moment you get close enough to investigate.

ACT: Watch for an answer to your signal.
Situation Description: A distant light answers your torch signal with two deliberate flashes.

ACT: Keep the distant light under observation.
Situation Description: After several minutes of watching, the light remains fixed and then fades.

Situation Name: A Thief Is Searching the Bags
ACT: Open the disturbed bags and inspect them immediately.
Situation Description: You catch a stranger quietly opening one of your bags.

Situation Name: A Thief Runs with Stolen Goods

Situation Description: A figure runs from the camp carrying something taken from your supplies.

Situation Name: An Animal Is Inside the Cargo

Situation Description: An animal is rummaging between the bags in search of food.

Situation Description: One of your bags has been cut open cleanly along the side.

ACT: Finish checking the cargo inventory and confirm what is missing.
Situation Description: Your count confirms that part of your cargo is gone.

Situation Name: A Loose Strap Caused the Noise

Situation Description: A cargo strap has come loose and several items have shifted.

Situation Name: A Stranger Is Watching the Cargo
ACT: Keep watch over the cargo without moving.
Situation Description: A person stands beyond the light and appears focused on your supplies.

Situation Name: The Intruder Approaches While You Pretend to Sleep

Situation Description: A person quietly approaches the cargo, believing you are still asleep.

ACT: Watch the bait from a safe distance.
Situation Description: A fox cautiously approaches the food and keeps glancing toward the camp.

Situation Name: A Wolf Watches from the Darkness

Situation Description: A wolf stands just beyond the firelight and watches without approaching.

ACT: Listen carefully for the animal's position.
Situation Description: More than one pair of eyes moves around the camp outside the firelight.

ACT: Approach the injured animal carefully enough to judge its condition.
Situation Description: You find an injured animal struggling to move near the edge of camp.

Situation Name: The Animal Retreats from Your Noise
ACT: Hold your ground and see how the animal reacts.
Situation Description: The animal moves farther away after hearing your attempt to scare it.

Situation Name: The Embers Can Still Be Saved

Situation Description: Beneath the ash, enough heat remains to rebuild the fire.

ACT: Inspect the fuel and try to restore the fire.
Situation Description: Most of the exposed firewood is soaked and difficult to use.

ACT: Inspect another part of the camp for storm damage.
Situation Description: One of the shelter ropes has broken and part of the cover is collapsing.

ACT: Inspect the nearest signs more closely.
Situation Description: Rainwater is beginning to soak through the protection around your supplies.

Situation Description: Water collects around the campsite faster than it can drain away.

ACT: Check whether the shelter will hold.
Situation Description: The reinforced shelter bends in the wind but remains stable.

ACT: Inspect the covered cargo as the rain worsens.
Situation Description: A section of the cargo cover tears and exposes goods to the rain.

Situation Description: You temporarily patch the tear to keep the rain away from the goods.

ACT: Decide the shelter is stable enough and return to rest beneath it.
Situation Description: You decide the shelter is stable enough and return to rest beneath it.

Situation Description: You decide that further searching is unlikely to help and return to the fire.

Situation Description: You remain awake for a while longer to see whether anything happens again.

Situation Description: You follow the rough trail into the darkness for a short distance.

Situation Description: You search the nearby area for whoever left the pack behind.

ACT: Stay with the traveller until the situation is settled.
Situation Description: Your help is enough for the traveller to recover and continue toward the road. Before leaving, they insist that you take a few coins for your trouble.

ACT: Stay with the wounded traveller a little longer and see whether they can continue.
Situation Description: The traveller is too weak to continue and remains near the fire until morning.

ACT: Ask one final question before ending the conversation.
Situation Description: Your questions reveal useful information about danger on the nearby road.

ACT: Keep questioning the traveller until you are satisfied with the answer.
Situation Description: The traveller answers your questions, but their story leaves you unconvinced.

ACT: Let the traveller remain by the fire a little longer.
Situation Description: The traveller spends a quiet while beside your fire before continuing their journey, mentioning unusually strong demand for certain goods along the road ahead.

ACT: Watch the traveller leave before returning to rest.
Situation Description: The traveller accepts your refusal and disappears back into the night.

ACT: Make sure the merchant understands the route.
Situation Description: With your directions, the merchant finds the road again. Before leaving, they repay the favour by mentioning a recent shortage and unusual prices in the settlement they came from.

ACT: Press the stranger for one final answer.
Situation Description: After being questioned, the stranger gives a believable explanation and mentions recent trade activity on the nearby road before moving on.

ACT: Hold your ground and give the suspicious stranger one last chance to answer.
Situation Description: The stranger refuses to explain themselves and slowly retreats into the darkness.

ACT: Hold your warning and watch how the stranger responds.
Situation Description: The stranger decides not to approach further and leaves the area.

ACT: Stand your ground and finish the confrontation.
Situation Description: The armed stranger decides the confrontation is not worth the risk and withdraws.

ACT: Refuse to back away and defend yourself as the armed stranger closes in.
Situation Description: The stranger attacks, forcing a dangerous struggle before the threat finally ends.

ACT: Keep observing until their intentions are clear.
Situation Description: By watching from concealment, you learn that the strangers are merchants discussing shortages and prices in a nearby settlement.

Situation Name: The Cry Leads to an Injured Traveller
ACT: Continue carefully toward the source of distress.
Situation Description: You find the person in distress and bring them back toward the safety of the fire.

ACT: Approach the cry carefully, ready to pull back if something feels wrong.
Situation Description: The call for help leads you toward people waiting in ambush, forcing you to retreat.

ACT: Finish checking the abandoned belongings.
Situation Description: Clues inside the abandoned belongings reveal who carried them and where they may have gone. Nearby, separate from the pack, you also find a sealed waterskin with no identifying mark.

Situation Name: The Human Tracks Lead to a Traveller
ACT: Follow the tracks a little farther.
Situation Description: The footprints lead to a lone traveller resting a short distance from your camp. After a short conversation, they share what they recently saw along the road and in nearby markets.

ACT: Follow the human tracks only far enough to confirm where they lead.
Situation Description: The footprints continue toward the road until you decide not to follow farther.

Situation Name: The Blood Leads to an Injured Traveller
ACT: Continue along the blood trail.
Situation Description: The trail ends at an injured traveller hiding nearby.

Situation Name: The Blood Leads to an Injured Animal
ACT: Follow the blood trail until you can identify what is injured.
Situation Description: The trail ends at a wounded animal resting beneath cover.

ACT: Keep the hidden person in sight and demand an answer.
Situation Description: The figure runs before answering and disappears into the darkness.

ACT: Hold your position and give them a chance to respond.
Situation Description: The person reveals themselves and explains why they were watching the camp, mentioning useful trade activity they recently saw on the road.

Situation Name: The Stranger Refuses to Explain Your Name
ACT: Demand one last explanation.
Situation Description: The stranger refuses to explain how they know you and leaves before you can stop them.

Situation Name: No One Answers the Second Call
ACT: Wait for a final response to your call.
Situation Description: Your second call receives no response. After several quiet minutes, you return to rest.

ACT: Hold your position and give them a chance to respond.
Situation Description: A nervous stranger steps from hiding after your second call and, once calm, shares a useful piece of information about nearby trade.

Situation Name: The Returned Signal Leads to a Traveller
ACT: Follow the returned signal to its source.
Situation Description: Following the signal brings you to a lost traveller trying to find the road. After you help them regain their bearings, they offer you a few coins in thanks.

ACT: Search a little farther beyond the lantern.
Situation Description: You find no trace of the lantern's owner and eventually return to camp.

Situation Name: The Vanished Light Is Never Found
ACT: Check the place where the light disappeared.
Situation Description: You search where the light disappeared but find nothing that explains what you saw.

Situation Description: Blocked from escaping cleanly, the thief drops what they took and runs.

ACT: Keep the thief blocked even as they try to force their way past you.
Situation Description: The trapped thief lashes out before finally escaping into the darkness.

Situation Name: You Catch Up with the Thief
ACT: Push the chase for a little longer.
Situation Description: You catch the thief before they disappear and recover what they were carrying.

ACT: Continue the attempt a little longer before deciding whether to stop.
Situation Description: The thief is faster in the darkness and disappears with the stolen goods.

ACT: Hold your demand and wait for the thief's answer.
Situation Description: Faced directly, the thief gives back what they took and retreats.

ACT: Keep demanding the stolen goods back as the thief looks for a way out.
Situation Description: The thief ignores your demand and bolts into the darkness.

ACT: Let the thief go and return your attention to camp.
Situation Description: You let the thief go and the footsteps quickly fade into the night.

ACT: Finish searching the area for the missing cargo.
Situation Description: You recover most of the missing items scattered or hidden around the camp.

ACT: Search the area one final time before accepting that the cargo is gone.
Situation Description: Your search finds no trace of the lost cargo.

ACT: Check the repair before leaving the cargo.
Situation Description: Your repair prevents any further loss from the damaged bag.

ACT: Inspect the secured cargo one last time.
Situation Description: All loose goods are secured and the camp becomes quiet again.

ACT: Keep waiting for the intruder to return.
Situation Description: Your patience pays off when the intruder approaches the supplies again and reveals themselves.

ACT: Stay beside the cargo a little longer before returning to rest.
Situation Description: You wait beside the cargo, but nothing else approaches before morning.

ACT: Keep the watcher at a distance until they leave.
Situation Description: Once confronted, the stranger backs away from your supplies and leaves.

ACT: Keep making noise from a safe distance and give the animal room to retreat.
Situation Description: The animal recoils at the noise and disappears into the darkness.

ACT: Advance more aggressively and try to force the large animal away.
Situation Description: Instead of fleeing, the large animal reacts aggressively and charges before eventually retreating.

Situation Description: You keep only a small flame alive. It gives you enough light to see the edge of camp without using the fuel needed for a full fire.

ACT: Rely on the temporary fix and avoid disturbing it further.
Situation Description: The remaining embers provide light for a while, but they fade sooner than you hoped and leave the camp dark again.

ACT: Search beneath the cart, shelter, and nearby cover for anything dry enough to burn.
Situation Description: You search beneath the cart, shelter, and nearby cover for anything dry enough to burn.

ACT: Examine what you found closely enough to make use of the clue.
Situation Description: Beneath the cart and nearby cover, you find enough dry firewood to rebuild the fire and still keep a small usable bundle for later.

Situation Name: No Dry Kindling Can Be Found
ACT: Wait a little longer, then accept that no clearer answer is coming.
Situation Description: You search beneath the cart, shelter, and nearby cover, but everything you find is too damp to burn. You return to the fire without usable kindling.

Situation Name: Reinforce the Shelter Instead of Replacing the Rope
ACT: Brace the damaged section with available materials rather than relying on the broken rope.
Situation Description: You brace the damaged section with available materials rather than relying on the broken rope.

ACT: Trust the repair and wait through the remaining danger.
Situation Description: The extra braces steady the damaged section. It continues to strain in the wind, but the shelter remains standing through the worst of the storm.

ACT: Rely on the temporary fix and avoid disturbing it further.
Situation Description: The improvised braces hold for a while, but the wet ground and strong wind slowly loosen them. The shelter remains usable, though it will need proper repair.

Situation Name: Move the Most Valuable Goods Under Shelter
ACT: Prioritize the most valuable cargo and move it into the driest part of the camp.
Situation Description: You prioritize the most valuable cargo and move it into the driest part of the camp.

ACT: Trust the repair and wait through the remaining danger.
Situation Description: Moving the most valuable goods under the driest part of the shelter works. The rain reaches the outer cargo, but the items you prioritized remain protected.

Situation Name: Only the Most Valuable Goods Stay Dry
ACT: Rely on the temporary fix and avoid disturbing it further.
Situation Description: You protect the most valuable goods, but there is not enough dry space for everything. Some less important cargo remains exposed to the rain.

Situation Name: Inspect the Shelter One More Time
ACT: Check the reinforced shelter carefully before trusting it for the rest of the storm.
Situation Description: You check the reinforced shelter carefully before trusting it for the rest of the storm.

Situation Name: The Shelter Inspection Finds the Weak Point
ACT: Examine what you found closely enough to make use of the clue.
Situation Description: Your final inspection reveals where the strain is concentrated. The reinforcement is holding, but you now know which support needs proper repair when the storm is over.

Situation Name: The Shelter Check Finds No New Problem
ACT: Wait a little longer, then accept that no clearer answer is coming.
Situation Description: You inspect every rope, brace, and weak point once more. Nothing has worsened, and the reinforced shelter appears stable enough for the rest of the storm.

Situation Name: The Traveller Pays for Your Hospitality
ACT: Give the person a moment to respond to your decision.
Situation Description: Before leaving, the traveller thanks you for sharing the safety and warmth of your camp and leaves a few coins behind.

Situation Name: The Traveller Leaves a Quiet Warning
ACT: Give the person a moment to respond to your decision.
Situation Description: The traveller accepts your decision and turns away from the fire. Before leaving, they quietly warn you that the road ahead has been unsettled after dark.

Situation Name: The Merchant Pays for Your Help
ACT: Give the person a moment to respond to your decision.
Situation Description: Grateful for the directions, the merchant presses a few coins into your hand before continuing toward the road.

ACT: Give the person a moment to respond to your decision.
Situation Description: The stranger studies you for a moment, then decides not to test your warning. They back away slowly and disappear into the darkness.

ACT: Give the person a moment to respond to your decision.
Situation Description: By observing a little longer, you realize the group is only trying to decide which road to take. They eventually move on without approaching your camp.

ACT: Follow through with your decision to search the Abandoned Belongings.
Situation Description: Beneath the abandoned belongings you uncover one bulky trade good that appears to have been left behind when the campsite was deserted.

ACT: Give the person a moment to respond to your decision.
Situation Description: When you challenge them about knowing your name, the stranger refuses to explain. They step back into the darkness and leave before you can learn more.

Situation Name: The Returned Signal Leads to an Empty Road
ACT: Follow through with your decision to follow the Returned Light Signal.
Situation Description: You follow the direction of the returned light, but reach only an empty stretch of road. Whoever signalled has already moved on, leaving no clear trace behind.

Situation Name: A Dropped Bundle Lies Beyond the Lantern
ACT: Follow through with your decision to search Beyond the Extinguished Lantern.
Situation Description: Searching beyond the extinguished lantern turns up a small dropped bundle of trade goods before the trail goes cold.

Situation Name: The Vanished Light Leaves Fresh Tracks
ACT: Follow through with your decision to follow Where the Light Vanished.
Situation Description: You search where the light disappeared and find fresh tracks leading toward the road. The person carrying the light is gone, but the signs confirm that the light was real.

ACT: Continue the attempt a little longer before deciding whether to stop.
Situation Description: Despite your response, the thief finds an opening and escapes into the darkness before the encounter can develop further.

Situation Name: A Small Item Was Lost Before the Repair
ACT: Secure what you can and accept that some cargo remains exposed.
Situation Description: The damaged bag is secure now, but your inspection shows that one small item slipped out before you completed the repair.

Situation Name: The Remaining Cargo Is Secure, but Something Is Missing
ACT: Secure what you can and accept that some cargo remains exposed.
Situation Description: You tighten every strap and secure what remains. Only afterward do you notice that one small item must have fallen out during the earlier disturbance.

Situation Name: The Cargo Watcher Took Something Before Leaving
ACT: Secure what you can and accept that some cargo remains exposed.
Situation Description: The watcher backs away after being confronted, but a quick check shows that they managed to take one small item before you noticed them.

ACT: Hold your position and watch how the animal responds.
Situation Description: You stay still and observe. Instead of leaving, the animal cautiously edges closer to the firelight, sniffing the air before finally deciding to move on.

Situation Name: The Animal Takes the Food and Keeps Its Distance
ACT: Stay back and watch what the animal does with the food.
Situation Description: The animal takes the food but keeps its distance from your cargo and bedroll, eventually retreating into the darkness.

ACT: Hold your position and watch how the animal responds.
Situation Description: You give the animal space and move back toward camp. It watches your retreat but does not follow, eventually turning away on its own.

Situation Name: The Animal Tests Another Side of the Cargo
ACT: Hold your position and watch how the animal responds.
Situation Description: Blocked from the supplies, the animal circles once and searches for another opening. Finding none, it loses interest and moves away.

ACT: Hold your position and watch how the animal responds.
Situation Description: You leave the injured animal undisturbed. After resting for a while, it manages to stand and limp away from the edge of camp.

Situation Name: The Animal Waits Beyond the Fire
ACT: Hold your position and watch how the animal responds.
Situation Description: The stronger flames keep the animal at a distance. It lingers beyond the light for a while, then finally gives up and disappears.

Situation Name: The Retreating Animal Stops Once More
ACT: Hold your position and watch how the animal responds.
Situation Description: The animal pauses at the edge of sight and looks back toward camp. After a tense moment it continues away and does not return.

Situation Name: The Fire Stays Weak Despite the Protected Embers
ACT: Rely on the temporary fix and avoid disturbing it further.
Situation Description: Your effort preserves some heat, but the fire never grows strong again. You finish the night with only a weak glow for warmth and light.

Situation Name: The Reserved Fuel Burns Too Quickly
ACT: Hold your ground and wait.
Situation Description: The protected fuel catches easily and restores the flames, but there is less of it than expected. The fire burns strongly for a short time before settling back to a weak glow.

Situation Name: Giving Up Leaves Only a Faint Glow
ACT: Rely on the temporary fix and avoid disturbing it further.
Situation Description: Once you stop trying to rebuild the fire, the remaining embers continue to fade. A faint glow survives for a while, but it provides little warmth.

ACT: Rely on the temporary fix and avoid disturbing it further.
Situation Description: The replaced rope keeps the shelter standing, but every strong gust pulls the repair tight. It survives the storm, though only just.

Situation Name: Some Outer Cargo Still Gets Wet
ACT: Secure what you can and accept that some cargo remains exposed.
Situation Description: You secure the exposed goods as quickly as possible, but rain reaches a small part of the outer cargo before everything can be moved under cover.

Situation Name: The Higher Ground Is Difficult but Safe
ACT: Follow through with your decision to move the Camp to Higher Ground.
Situation Description: Moving the camp is slow and awkward in the storm, but the new ground stays above the rising water and gives you a safe place to finish the night.

Situation Name: You Escape the Flood but Lose Some Cargo
ACT: Keep moving away from the flooded campsite until the immediate weather danger has passed.
Situation Description: You abandon the campsite before the water traps you. In the hurried departure, one small piece of cargo is lost to the mud and darkness.

Situation Name: Waiting Out the Storm Costs Rest
ACT: Stay sheltered and wait to see whether the storm causes another problem.
Situation Description: The shelter remains safe, but the storm takes a long time to weaken. By the time you can settle properly again, part of the night has been lost.

Situation Name: The Patch Holds, but Some Cargo Is Already Wet
ACT: Secure what you can and accept that some cargo remains exposed.
Situation Description: Your patch stops most of the rain, but a small amount of cargo was soaked before you could seal the torn cover.

Situation Name: The Shelter Survives, but the Night Is Uncomfortable
ACT: Rely on the temporary fix and avoid disturbing it further.
Situation Description: The shelter remains standing, but the strained supports creak through every gust. You stay dry enough, though the rest of the night is uneasy.

ACT: Follow through with your decision to return to Rest After Finding Nothing.
Situation Description: You turn back toward the fire after finding no clear source for the disturbance. Near the edge of camp, however, you notice a small bundle that seems to have been dropped in the darkness.

Situation Name: A Late Traveller Finally Steps Forward
ACT: Wait a little longer and see whether the unseen person reveals themselves.
Situation Description: Just as you are about to give up waiting, a cautious traveller finally steps into view. They explain that they were unsure whether the camp was safe and, before leaving, mention a useful trade condition on the road ahead.

ACT: Follow through with your decision to respect the Warning.
Situation Description: You respect the warning and keep your distance. After several tense moments, the unseen person withdraws and the area around camp becomes quiet again.

ACT: Remain by the fire and listen to the whispering.
Situation Description: You remain beside the fire as the quiet voices continue somewhere beyond the light. After a moment, it becomes clear that more than one person is speaking.

ACT: Stay by the fire and listen for any sign that the voices are still nearby.
Situation Description: You wait beside the fire, but the whispering abruptly stops. No one approaches, and the darkness around the camp becomes quiet again.

Situation Name: A Figure Moves Closer to the Firelight
ACT: Stay in the firelight and watch the nearby figure.
Situation Description: After several tense moments, a lone figure moves closer to the camp but stops just beyond the edge of the firelight.

ACT: Track the movement from beside the fire.
Situation Description: You stay beside the fire and wait. After a while, faint movement circles beyond the light without coming any closer.

Situation Name: Another Cry Comes from the Darkness
ACT: Stay put and listen for the voice again.
Situation Description: You remain beside the fire until another distant cry carries through the night, confirming that someone or something is still out there.

ACT: Keep waiting while watching the weakening fire.
Situation Description: You stay beside the fire and watch the weak flames sink lower until only a bed of glowing embers remains.

ACT: Watch for the strange light to appear again.
Situation Description: You remain beside the fire, and after a tense wait the distant light appears again between the trees.

Situation Name: An Animal Lingers Beyond the Camp
ACT: Keep watch for the animal from the camp.
Situation Description: You stay beside the fire until a shape moves at the edge of the darkness, revealing that an animal has remained nearby.

Situation Name: Nothing Comes Closer to the Fire
ACT: Wait a little longer beside the fire.
Situation Description: You remain beside the fire and wait, but the unknown presence that disturbed the night never comes close enough to reveal itself.

Situation Name: The Torch Reveals No Clear Source
ACT: Sweep the torchlight over the area once more.
Situation Description: The torchlight reaches across the nearby ground, but nothing obvious remains within sight.

ACT: Keep listening for another cry before deciding the voice is gone.
Situation Description: You listen carefully for another call, but the night stays silent and gives you no clearer direction.

ACT: Wait quietly for the footsteps to return.
Situation Description: You wait for the footsteps to begin again, but the area around the camp becomes completely still.

ACT: Hold the torch signal a little longer and watch for an answer.
Situation Description: You hold the torch high and wait, but no light answers from the darkness.

ACT: Keep watching the distant light until it disappears from view.
Situation Description: You watch from the safety of the camp until the distant light slowly disappears between the trees.

ACT: Keep guarding the cargo and wait.
Situation Description: You keep watch over the supplies, but no one comes close enough to threaten the cargo again.

Situation Name: A Lone Animal Moves Near the Camp
ACT: Stay still and watch the lone animal at the edge of the camp.
Situation Description: A single shape moves through the darkness near the camp before hesitating at the edge of the firelight.

ACT: Keep making noise and watch whether the animal retreats or stands its ground.
Situation Description: The noise makes the animal pause, but instead of fleeing it remains just beyond the firelight.

Situation Name: A Larger Animal Finds the Bait
ACT: Stay back and watch what approaches the bait.
Situation Description: Movement approaches the food, but the shape that emerges is larger than you expected.

ACT: Check whether any usable fuel remains after protecting the embers.
Situation Description: You protect the last heat from the wind, but most of the nearby fuel has already become too wet to burn easily.

ACT: Search the damp firewood for anything dry enough to burn.
Situation Description: Most of the exposed wood is damp, but you find a small amount of protected fuel that may still be usable.

Situation Name: Water Begins Gathering Around the Shelter
ACT: Check the ground around the shelter while tightening the supports.
Situation Description: While securing the shelter, you notice water collecting around the campsite faster than expected.

Situation Name: Rain Starts Reaching the Covered Goods
ACT: Inspect the cargo covers again as the rain grows heavier.
Situation Description: Despite your precautions, water begins working through the cargo protection and threatens the exposed goods.

Situation Name: The Animal Retreats After a Standoff
ACT: Hold your ground without advancing and wait out the standoff.
Situation Description: The animal resists for a moment, then finally backs away and disappears beyond the edge of the camp.

ACT: Acknowledge the hunger and decide what to do.
Situation Description: Hunger pulls you out of an uneasy rest and refuses to let you settle again. Your stomach tightens painfully, and the thought of the food packed among your supplies becomes harder to ignore as the minutes pass.

ACT: Deal with the thirst before trying to rest again.
Situation Description: You wake with a dry mouth and a persistent thirst that makes it difficult to rest. The night air offers little relief, and your attention keeps returning to the water you still have or the lack of it.

ACT: Stop fighting the exhaustion and assess your condition.
Situation Description: The strain of the road finally catches up with you. Even at rest your muscles feel heavy, your thoughts come slowly, and the effort of the journey lingers in every movement.

ACT: Take a small portion of food from your supplies.
Situation Description: You decide that a little food is worth more than another hour of restless hunger.

ACT: Turn over and try to sleep through the hunger.
Situation Description: You decide not to spend food and try to force yourself back to sleep.

ACT: Get up and busy yourself with small tasks around camp.
Situation Description: Rather than eat, you check straps, tidy the fire, and keep your hands occupied.

Situation Name: A Small Meal Settles Your Stomach
ACT: Eat slowly and wait to see whether it is enough.
Situation Description: The small meal takes the edge off the hunger and your body begins to relax again.

ACT: Lie still a little longer and see whether the feeling passes.
Situation Description: Minutes pass, but the hunger only becomes harder to ignore.

Situation Name: Keeping Busy Helps for a While
ACT: Finish the small chores and see whether your mind settles.
Situation Description: The work distracts you for a while, though the hunger has not truly gone away.

ACT: Settle back down while the hunger is under control.
Situation Description: You return to your bedroll before the discomfort can return.

Situation Name: Give In and Eat After All
ACT: Stop fighting the hunger and take something from your supplies.
Situation Description: You finally decide that conserving the food is not worth losing the rest.

ACT: Stay awake a little longer and keep your hands busy.
Situation Description: You continue working around camp until tiredness begins to overpower the hunger.

ACT: Close your eyes and return to sleep.
Situation Description: With the hunger eased, you settle back into a more comfortable rest.

Situation Name: A Late Meal Finally Lets You Rest
ACT: Finish the small meal and return to bed.
Situation Description: The food finally quiets your stomach enough for sleep to return.

Situation Name: The Hunger Costs You Some Rest
ACT: Return to bed once you are too tired to keep busy.
Situation Description: You eventually sleep, but the time spent fighting the hunger leaves the rest less useful than it should have been.

ACT: Take a measured drink from your water supply.
Situation Description: You decide that a little water is worth more than another hour of restless thirst.

ACT: Ignore the dry throat and try to sleep without drinking.
Situation Description: You keep the water stored away and try to rest despite the discomfort.

Situation Name: Step into the Cooler Night Air
ACT: Leave the bedroll for a moment and cool down beside the camp.
Situation Description: You step away from the heat of the fire and let the cooler night air settle you.

ACT: Drink slowly and wait for the dryness to fade.
Situation Description: The water eases the thirst and your thoughts become less distracted.

ACT: Wait a little longer and see whether the discomfort passes.
Situation Description: The dryness only becomes harder to ignore, and sleep feels farther away.

Situation Name: The Cool Air Helps a Little
ACT: Stay outside the bedroll until you feel calmer.
Situation Description: The cooler air offers some relief, though it does not truly satisfy the thirst.

ACT: Settle back down while the thirst is under control.
Situation Description: You return to the bedroll before the discomfort can return.

ACT: Stop conserving the water and take a drink.
Situation Description: You finally decide that the lost rest is costing more than the water.

ACT: Stay in the cool air a little longer before returning to bed.
Situation Description: You remain outside the bedroll until tiredness begins to outweigh the thirst.

ACT: Close your eyes and return to sleep.
Situation Description: With the thirst eased, you settle into rest again.

Situation Name: The Drink Finally Lets You Rest
ACT: Finish the drink and return to bed.
Situation Description: The water settles the discomfort enough for sleep to return.

Situation Name: The Thirst Costs You Some Rest
ACT: Return to bed once you are too tired to stay awake.
Situation Description: You eventually sleep, but the time spent fighting the thirst leaves the rest less useful than it should have been.

ACT: Stop resisting and let yourself sink into the bedroll.
Situation Description: You decide that nothing around camp matters more than finally resting.

ACT: Force yourself up for one final check of the camp.
Situation Description: Despite the exhaustion, you decide to make sure the fire, cargo, and shelter are secure first.

Situation Name: Sit by the Fire for a Moment
ACT: Stay awake by the fire until your thoughts settle.
Situation Description: You sit quietly beside the fire and give yourself a moment to recover before lying down.

ACT: Let your body relax and stop fighting the fatigue.
Situation Description: The moment you lie down, the exhaustion pulls you toward deep sleep.

Situation Name: Fatigue Makes the Camp Check Difficult
ACT: Finish the check even though your attention is fading.
Situation Description: You catch yourself missing small details and moving more slowly than usual.

Situation Name: The Quiet Fire Clears Your Head
ACT: Stay beside the fire until you feel steady enough to sleep.
Situation Description: A few quiet minutes help your thoughts settle, even if your body remains exhausted.

ACT: Stop resisting and allow the rest to take over.
Situation Description: You stop checking the camp and finally give your body the rest it has been asking for.

ACT: Push through the fatigue long enough to secure the most important things.
Situation Description: You use the last of your focus to tighten the cargo and check the shelter before lying down.

Situation Name: Return to Bed Once You Feel Steadier
ACT: Leave the fire and settle down before the fatigue becomes worse.
Situation Description: You decide not to waste the brief calm and return to your bedroll.

ACT: Close your eyes and let the exhaustion take over.
Situation Description: Sleep comes almost immediately and the camp remains quiet around you.

Situation Name: The Extra Check Costs You Time
ACT: Lie down once the camp is finally secure.
Situation Description: The camp is safer, but fighting the exhaustion costs you time that should have been spent resting.

Situation Name: You Settle Down After the Pause
ACT: Return to sleep while your thoughts are finally calm.
Situation Description: The brief pause is enough to settle you, and the exhaustion soon carries you into sleep.

Situation Name: The Movement Belongs to a Person
ACT: Keep the figure in sight and judge what they are doing.
Situation Description: Following the disturbance, you catch sight of a person moving where the earlier rustling came from. The movement and the figure are clearly connected.

Situation Name: The Animal Is Close to Camp
ACT: Watch the animal carefully before deciding how to respond.
Situation Description: Your investigation leads you to the source of the cry: an animal lingering just beyond the camp, alert and watching your movements.

Situation Name: A Thief Breaks from the Cargo
ACT: Keep the intruder in sight before they can escape.
Situation Description: As you investigate the disturbed supplies, a person breaks away from the cargo and tries to slip into the darkness, confirming that someone was searching your goods.

Situation Name: The Movement Has a Human Rhythm
ACT: Keep listening until you can place the person more precisely.
Situation Description: The rustling settles into the measured rhythm of careful footsteps. Someone is moving around the edge of the camp.

ACT: Keep the torch trained on the figure.
Situation Description: The torchlight catches a human silhouette at the edge of the darkness. Whoever was nearby freezes for a moment instead of stepping into the light.

ACT: Keep the light on the animal and watch its reaction.
Situation Description: The torchlight finds the source of the animal sounds: a dark shape watching from just beyond the camp.

ACT: Inspect the direction of the tracks before following them.
Situation Description: Fresh human footprints lead in the same direction as the voice you heard, tying the cry to someone moving near the camp.

ACT: Study where the footprints lead from the disturbed ground.
Situation Description: Fresh human footprints cross the place where you heard movement and continue into the darkness, confirming that a person caused at least part of the disturbance.

ACT: Track the figure with the torchlight.
Situation Description: The torch sweeps across the trees and catches a human figure moving exactly where you heard the earlier disturbance.

ACT: Listen carefully and fix the direction of the voice.
Situation Description: The voice comes again, weaker but clearer this time, allowing you to place where the distressed person is calling from.

Situation Name: Blood Marks the Route of the Movement
ACT: Inspect the blood trail before deciding whether to follow.
Situation Description: Near the place where the movement passed, you find fresh drops of blood leading away into the darkness.

ACT: Inspect the tracks around the disturbed supplies.
Situation Description: Fresh human footprints circle the cargo and lead away from the camp, strongly suggesting that someone approached your supplies while you slept.

Situation Name: A Trail Continues Beneath the Light's Path
ACT: Follow the disturbed ground for a short distance.
Situation Description: Scuffed soil and broken vegetation continue in the same direction as the strange light, leaving a trail you can follow away from camp.

Situation Name: The Cry Leads to a Wounded Traveller
ACT: Approach carefully and assess the traveller's condition.
Situation Description: Following the direction of the cry, you find a wounded traveller close to camp. Their injuries explain the distressed voice that woke you.

ACT: Remain beside the weakening fire and see whether the embers hold.
Situation Description: You stay beside the weakening fire without adding more fuel, watching to see whether the remaining flames can hold on by themselves.

ACT: Study the tracks closely before deciding whether they are worth following.
Situation Description: You kneel beside the prints and study their size, depth, spacing, and direction, trying to judge what kind of animal passed near camp and how recently it was here.

Situation Name: Mark the Tracks and Return to Camp
ACT: Memorize the direction of the trail and return to the safety of the fire.
Situation Description: You decide not to follow an unseen animal through the darkness. Instead, you mark the direction of the tracks and return to camp while you still know exactly where you are.

Situation Name: The Tracks Belong to a Large Predator
ACT: Use what you learned from the tracks and return to camp.
Situation Description: The deep prints and long stride belong to a large predator. Knowing what passed nearby is warning enough, and you return to camp instead of following it into the dark.

Situation Name: The Tracks Belong to a Small Forager
ACT: Leave the harmless trail alone and return to camp.
Situation Description: The prints are small and light, belonging to a harmless foraging animal that likely passed through looking for scraps. With no real threat nearby, you return to rest.

Situation Name: The Tracks Are Too Disturbed to Read
ACT: Stop trying to identify the animal and return to camp.
Situation Description: The prints overlap with older marks and disturbed soil. You cannot identify the animal with confidence, so you decide not to follow an uncertain trail at night.

Situation Name: The Trail Stays Away from Camp
ACT: Keep the marked direction in mind and return to rest.
Situation Description: From the direction and spacing of the tracks, it is clear the animal was moving away from the campsite rather than toward it. You return to the fire reassured.

ACT: Listen once more, then choose not to pursue the unseen animal.
Situation Description: A branch shifts somewhere along the marked direction, confirming the animal is still moving through the area. It does not approach camp, and you choose not to chase it.

ACT: Watch the marked trail briefly before returning to rest.
Situation Description: You keep the trail under observation from camp, but nothing follows the tracks back toward the fire. Eventually you let the night settle again.

Situation Name: Let the Animal Take the Bait
ACT: Stay back and let the animal use the bait you already placed.
Situation Description: The bait is already in position, so you do not offer anything more. You remain still and watch to see whether the animal takes the food and leaves the camp alone.

Situation Name: The Movement Fades into the Distance
ACT: Listen until you are sure the movement is leaving the area.
Situation Description: You wait without pursuing it. The faint rustling gradually moves farther from camp until the night becomes still again.

ACT: Wait for the distant voice to return one more time.
Situation Description: You remain awake and listen, but the cry never comes again. With no direction to follow and no further sign of distress, you eventually return to rest.

ACT: Keep watching the supplies for another disturbance.
Situation Description: You wait beside the cargo, but nothing touches the bags again. Whatever caused the earlier noise does not return before the camp settles.

Situation Name: The Footsteps Continue Down the Road
ACT: Listen until the footsteps are clearly moving away.
Situation Description: The footsteps resume at a distance and continue past the camp rather than toward it. Whoever was walking nearby appears to be travelling on.

Situation Name: The Strange Light Disappears Beyond the Trees
ACT: Watch the last place where the light was visible.
Situation Description: The distant light appears once more between the trees, then moves steadily away until it disappears from sight. It never approaches the camp.

ACT: Listen to the direction of the animal sounds before returning to rest.
Situation Description: The animal calls again from farther away, then gradually fade into the distance. Whatever animal passed nearby is moving away from camp.

ACT: Stay quiet until the voices are clearly leaving.
Situation Description: The whispering continues for a short while beyond the firelight, then the voices drift farther away. The unseen people decide not to approach your camp.
